summary.intent: Run the GSD manager to discuss phases 42–44 (API unpin integrity, FUSE write durability, IPNS conflict handling) and then plan and execute Phase 42 through all waves.
summary.outcome: Phases 42–44 were fully discussed with CONTEXT.md files committed. Phase 42 was planned (8 plans) and executed through Wave 2 (5/8 plans complete): schema/metrics foundation, quota reconcile, guardedUnpin security core, live DB migrations, and Grafana alert all landed. Wave 3 was dispatched but not yet complete at session end.

repo: The unpin endpoint (POST /ipfs/unpin) is protected only by JwtAuthGuard with open signup — any account holder can submit arbitrary CIDs; the handler never reads req.user and passes the CID string directly to Kubo pin/rm, making it a cross-tenant data-destruction surface.

Kubo v0.40 in staging runs with the 'server' profile and swarm port 4001 exposed publicly (docker/docker-compose.staging.yml:62-72), meaning all pinned CIDs are broadcast via public DHT provider records and harvestable by crawlers.
Kubo API (port 5001) is loopback-only since Phase 29 — the public API endpoint is the only path in.
Writable-share saves drop prunedCids without calling unpin — there is no live cross-user legitimate unpin path in the current codebase.
BYO-IPFS delete flows only remove the pinned_cids row advisory; provider.unpin is never called, leaving BYO pins unmanaged on deletion.
eslint already ignores .planning and .claude directories; .prettierignore was missing, causing prettier to mangle markdown tables in planning files during pre-commit.
vault.module.ts required a local IPFS_PROVIDER useFactory (no re-export from IpfsModule) to avoid a circular import when PendingUnpin was added to forFeature.

code.finding: Kubo 'server' profile keeps full public DHT participation — disables only local-network discovery, not swarm/DHT. Port 4001 is publicly exposed tcp+udp.

guardedUnpin added in 42-03: Postgres advisory xact lock on hash(cid) → row delete → refcount → conditional pending_unpins insert → Kubo pin/rm post-commit. Cross-user attempt increments metric and emits audit log at warn level, returns 200.
58 total tests after 42-03 added 6 guardedUnpin cases (RED→GREEN TDD gates honored).
New entity @Entity('pending_unpins') — columns id (uuid PK), cid (varchar 255), created_at; no user_id; unique index on cid.
Three new Prometheus metrics added: unpinCrossUserAttempts, driftOrphanedPinsTotal, pendingUnpinsGauge.
New alert in 'CipherBox Security' rule group: rate(cipherbox_unpin_cross_user_attempts_total[5m]) > 0, using existing placeholder-UID convention.
Web unpin calls swallow errors with .catch(logger.warn) — no response code is read, confirming silent 2XX is safe for existing callers.

workflow: GSD manager on Claude Code runs plan/execute inline (not backgrounded) because backgrounded agents cannot nest subagents for plan-checker and worktree isolation.
Wave-based parallel execution uses isolated git worktrees per plan; node_modules in agent worktrees must be cleaned before the post-wave merge helper will accept them.
Post-merge gates should be run with direct jest invocation rather than pnpm scripts that forward '--' as flags, which causes jest to treat the filter as a positional regex.
Blocking migration checkpoints auto-approve under --auto once automated SQL verification passes (to_regclass() query confirming schema objects exist).
1Password commit signing can stall non-interactively; having a retry path (or pre-authorizing the signing key) is needed for autonomous plan commits.
Prettier must be added to .prettierignore for .planning and .claude directories to prevent it from mangling markdown tables in pre-commit hooks.

friction: Session limit hit mid-Phase 42 discussion, interrupting the conversation (reset at 3:50am Europe/Berlin timezone).
Phase 42 plan commit silently failed twice (HEAD unchanged) due to 1Password signing requiring interactive authorization — required retry and recovery.
Phase 44 context commit initially did not land (git log still showed phase 43 as HEAD); required explicit retry with visible output to diagnose.

Jest invoked via pnpm script with forwarded '--' treated the filter as a positional regex, silently running the wrong test scope.
